business_scope.primary_industry_name: Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage

Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement between the EU and Egypt (2004)
Agreement establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018) and its Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and its Executive Regulations; Beneficial ownership disclosure requirements under GAFI's UBO declaration forms; Notary Public Law No. 68 of 1947.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of the full passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport administration or general civil registry authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille as recognized in Egypt (2022) or Egyptian consular legalization if the issuing state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or active status certificate for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies register or chamber of commerce in the corporate shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each corporate shareholder approving the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, the UBO declarations, and the appointed directors/managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and notary public in the corporate shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Residential address and source-of-funds proof for each UBO, including utility bill, bank reference letter, and asset statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider, municipal authority, or issuing bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed power of attorney in favor of the Egyptian incorporation agent, including authority to file UBO declarations and name reservation documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of signing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening under Law No. 80 of 2002 and FATF Recommendation 12. Every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized signatory must be screened in real time against (i) the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit's domestic sanctions and terrorist designation lists, (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and relevant OFAC sectoral sanctions programs, (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and (v) national and international PEP databases covering senior political figures and their family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, is mandatory for any PEP or higher-risk jurisdiction, and any positive sanctions hit requires immediate suspensive reporting to the Egyptian AML/CFT Unit. The screening report must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Unified Electronic Company Registration and Name Reservation System (www.gafi.gov.eg), in coordination with the Commercial Registry at the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The LLC name must be registered in Arabic script as the official statutory name. A Latin/English transliteration may be filed as an additional trade name at the Commercial Registry, but it must faithfully render the Arabic name and must not be deceptively similar to an existing registered foreign name. The name shall include a descriptive corporate suffix, being 'Limited Liability Company' or its Arabic equivalent, and may include the company's stated purpose or a distinctive invented word, provided it does not violate Egyptian public order or religious sensitivities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days of a rejection notification, the authorized Egyptian representative may file a written administrative objection with the GAFI Companies Registration Dispute Committee, attaching the name-search report, transliteration alternatives, supporting trademark or authorization letters, and a legal memorandum showing compliance with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and its Executive Regulations. If the objection is denied or GAFI remains silent, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the State Council Administrative Court within 60 days from the final refusal. A new reservation for a distinct alternative name may be filed immediately without prejudice to the appeal if counsel determines that the objection cannot be resolved within the current reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a low-risk professional services firm carrying out ESG/carbon accounting and audit, a purely virtual mailbox or zero-footprint office is not acceptable for LLC incorporation. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical registered office in Egypt, with a verifiable address, lease or ownership instrument, and a local person authorized to receive process. A licensed serviced-office provider may satisfy this requirement only if it maintains a physical presence, a formal service agreement, and the client's statutory records are accessible at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15-20% in the first operating year for an entity classified as Low_Risk_Standard under AML/CFT banking-style risk scoring. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, or tax inspectors may carry out desk audits, unannounced registered-office visits, and CDD record inspections; frequency may increase after tax/VAT registration or if the UBO is a PEP or a higher-risk jurisdiction supervises the entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 concerning Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares, and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 138/2019 – Articles 1-12 (formation and registration of LLCs) and investment-related amendments under Law No. 72/2017; implementing executive regulations as issued through GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Services Center (One-Stop Shop), Companies Department, Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade, Arab Republic of Egypt.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Contract of Incorporation (Incorporation Agreement) being the LLC Memorandum and Articles of Association combined; submitted electronically through GAFI One-Stop Shop and registered in the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Law 159/1981 as amended in 2019. The founders freely determine the capital, which must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited into a temporary escrow bank account in the LLC's name at an Egyptian bank approved by GAFI, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate, and the funds are released upon issuance of the Commercial Registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the directors held immediately after incorporation, the board resolved: (1) the company is confirmed as validly incorporated under Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended and registered with GAFI; (2) the subscribed share capital stated in the Notarized Contract of Incorporation is hereby declared fully subscribed and paid; (3) the registered office is adopted at [address], Egypt; (4) the undersigned persons are appointed as directors and authorized signatories with the signing powers approved by the members; (5) the appointed directors are delegated to complete commercial registry, tax, social insurance, publication, and bank account opening formalities; and (6) the Chairman may execute all ancillary documents to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Activity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (online investor portal) and the Commercial Registry name database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the GAFI digital platform or attend the Investor Services Center; submit three proposed company names in order of preference; verify that the intended activity matches ISIC 7020 and does not require a pre-license from a sectoral regulator; obtain the official Name Reservation Certificate and ISIC classification approval.
required_dossiers: Founders' valid national IDs or passports
Power of attorney for the authorized representative (if applicable)
Declaration of business activity (ISIC 7020 – corporate sustainability, carbon auditing, and advisory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registration, the company may resubmit alternative names within 3 working days at no additional fee; if the activity classification is refused, submit amended descriptive documents showing that the activities are non-regulated professional services and appeal to the GAFI commercial registration committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Account Opening and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank operating through the GAFI One-Stop Shop banking window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate escrow bank account in the proposed LLC name; deposit the full cash subscription amount equal to the initial capital declared in the incorporation contract; obtain the bank's certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt) for submission with the incorporation file. If in-kind contributions are made, have a certified public accountant valuer prepare the valuation report as approved by the founders.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to incomplete documentation, the Notary Public must attest to the signature of all parties and re-submit; if the cash is in foreign currency, provide a currency exchange authorization from the Central Bank of Egypt or adjust currency to EGP; escalate to GAFI's banking liaison for inter-bank facilitation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Notary Public attached to GAFI One-Stop Shop or Ministry of Justice notary office in the relevant governorate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or their authorized attorneys must appear physically before the notary public to sign the incorporation contract; the notary authenticates signatures and statutory declarations; the contract is stamped and certified as an official instrument required for registration; any third-party witnesses required by GAFI procedures are also attested.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if signatory is a representative
Declaration of compliance with Investment Law No. 72/2017
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests amendments, the amendments are inserted into an addendum signed by all founders in the same notarial session; if an individual founder is unavailable, issue a notarized power of attorney from that founder's home jurisdiction through the Egyptian consulate; the notary's refusal can be appealed to the head of the notary department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop Registration Submission and Commercial Registration Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (One-Stop Shop) – Commercial Registry and Investor Licensing Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation contract together with all supporting dossiers through the GAFI online portal or in-person service window; pay the statutory registration fee, commercial registry fee, notary surcharge, and official gazette publication fees; GAFI will issue the certificate of incorporation, the Commercial Registration certificate, the tax card (ETA) from the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the initial social insurance registration from NSSA in a single coordinated workflow; the applicant collects all certificates at the OSS counters after the verification officer approves the electronic file.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or title deed proving registered office address
Legal opinion on office occupation (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency notice, the applicant must cure all noted items within 15 working days by filing supplementary declarations or revised notarial instruments; if the query relates to the registered office, provide additional lease authenticated documents; a third-party objection letter must be answered within 10 days; final administrative refusal can be appealed to the GAFI Dispute Resolution (Investor Grievance) Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance, Gazette Publication, and Final Corporate Seal Acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NSSA) through GAFI OSS; the Commercial Registry publication office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI automatically coordinates NSSA registration for all directors and employees; verify the NSSA registration declaration; arrange for the publication of the incorporation contract summary in the Official Gazette and the commercial registry bulletin; after final registration, obtain the corporate seal from a licensed engraver and open the permanent operating bank account with the escrow bank, releasing the escrow funds to the company's ordinary corporate account.
required_dossiers: Directors' IDs and proof of social insurance schedule
Bank account release authorization from the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NSSA data is inconsistent, file a curing notification through the OSS within 30 days with a joint declaration of directors; if the gazette publication is delayed, GAFI certifies the company exists and the applicant may complete any banking requirement using the certified commercial registration and notarized incorporation contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Safety, Civil Defense Clearance, and Office Premises Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Administration of Civil Protection, Ministry of Interior (Fire Safety Department), together with the local governorate administrative office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registered office lease and floor plan to the Civil Protection inspector; the inspector examines fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical load certificates; obtain the fire safety efficiency certificate and the administrative license for professional office use; for an office-only carbon advisory business, no industrial operating license is required, but the employer must maintain a workplace injury register and provide first-aid equipment per occupational safety standards.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease contract for the premises
Floor plan and building structural certificate
Electrical installation safety report (approved by licensed engineer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire clearance is denied, undertake the corrective works listed by the inspector and request re-inspection within 60 days; if the premises are structurally unsuitable, relocate the registered office and re-notify GAFI; an administrative appeal against an unreasonable denial may be filed with the Ministry of Interior's appellate committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Investor Licensing and Post-Formation Services Department; no industrial licensing body is applicable to ISIC 7020 professional advisory services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Office Trade License and Commercial Registration for Professional Business Advisory (no industrial operating license; entity remains a service provider under GAFI One-Stop Shop)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category [C] – Exempt from full EIA report for non-industrial administrative office activities; the entity is only required to file an environmental self-monitoring declaration if it introduces laboratory, high-energy equipment, or electronic waste streams, at which point it will be downgraded to Category B requiring an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office/professional use, no process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; if any incidental testing or calibration equipment is introduced, discharges to public sewer must comply with Law 4/1994, Law 48/1982, and Ministerial Decree 44/2000: BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, pH 6-9.5; office air quality must comply with workplace TLV standards for VOCs; e-waste and spent batteries must be routed to licensed recyclers exclusively.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate (certificate of fire suitability) from the General Administration of Civil Protection for the registered office; structural load inspection certificate for any archive-heavy storage room; occupational workplace clearance includes workplace hazard assessment, first-aid inventory, and incident reporting under Ministerial Decree 211/2003; no high-risk chemical or explosive clearance is required for ESG-carbon advisory operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, through the ETA Taxpayer Portal, VAT registration systems, and the Egyptian e-Invoicing Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Egyptian LLC must complete incorporation and commercial registration, obtain the tax card and unified tax registration number from the competent ETA tax office or electronic portal, and submit the constitutional documents, commercial register, registered address evidence, identification documents of authorized representatives, lease or ownership evidence, bank details where requested, and business activity information. VAT registration is required where the entity conducts taxable supplies and reaches the statutory registration threshold, or where voluntary registration is accepted by the ETA. A foreign entity without an Egyptian legal entity must generally register through its Egyptian permanent establishment, branch, local tax representative, or other legally recognized taxable presence where it conducts business in Egypt. The registration file should identify corporate income tax obligations, VAT obligations, payroll withholding obligations, and e-invoicing obligations. The ETA may conduct an address or activity verification before issuing or activating the tax registration. Taxpayers must maintain current registration data and notify the ETA of material changes, cessation, branch additions, or changes in authorized signatories.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not generally provide a United States-style check-the-box election for an Egyptian LLC, nor a general elective pass-through regime for ordinary LLCs. The LLC is normally subject to Egyptian corporate income tax at entity level, with distributions potentially subject to separate withholding or dividend tax rules. VAT registration may be mandatory upon exceeding the statutory threshold and may be available voluntarily below the threshold subject to ETA acceptance and compliance. Special tax treatment may arise from qualifying free-zone, investment-zone, or other incentive regimes, but those regimes require separate statutory eligibility and do not constitute a general entity-classification election. No broad Egyptian hybrid-mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Egyptian Value Added Tax Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of taxable supplies during the relevant statutory measurement period, generally measured by annual turnover. Voluntary registration may be available below the threshold subject to ETA procedures and approval. Certain goods and services may be exempt, zero-rated, or subject to special rates or schedules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Entities within the mandatory scope must issue electronic tax invoices for business-to-business transactions through the ETA e-Invoicing Portal. Implementation requires taxpayer onboarding, approved electronic signature or seal, structured invoice data, integration through an approved API or compliant ERP/accounting solution, and generation of the ETA-issued unique invoice identifier and digital validation or approval status. Invoices must be submitted to the ETA in accordance with the applicable technical timing and data requirements; cancellation, rejection, credit notes, and amendments must follow the portal workflow. Electronic receipts apply to covered business-to-consumer transactions under the ETA e-Receipt system. Export transactions and transactions with nonresident customers should be separately coded and supported by evidence of export or offshore use. Failure to issue, report, retain, or correctly authenticate electronic documents can result in VAT assessments, administrative penalties, denial of input-tax credits, and enforcement action.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods may qualify for zero-rated export treatment where they are exported outside Egypt under the VAT Law and customs procedures, with proof that the goods physically left Egypt and the export transaction is properly reported. Services supplied to a nonresident may qualify for zero-rating where the statutory conditions are satisfied, including that the recipient is outside Egypt and the service is used or enjoyed outside Egypt; services directly connected with Egyptian real estate, goods located in Egypt, or activities performed in Egypt may fail the offshore-service test. Carbon accounting, ESG advisory, audit, and offset-brokerage services should be analyzed by deliverable, place of performance, customer status, economic use, and the location of the underlying project or asset. A zero-rated invoice must state the applicable VAT treatment, and the taxpayer must retain contracts, customer and residency evidence, work product, correspondence, payment records, and evidence that the service benefit was outside Egypt. Input VAT refunds generally require a valid VAT registration, compliant tax invoices or customs documents, proof of payment and business use, accurate VAT returns, and reconciliation of the claim to accounting records and e-invoice data.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration or equivalent electronically accepted export record
Commercial invoice identifying the Egyptian exporter, foreign customer, goods, value, currency, and zero-rated treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, or other carrier evidence where applicable
Evidence of customs release and physical exit from Egypt
Foreign customer contract, purchase order, and proof of nonresident status
Bank receipt, inward remittance evidence, or other permitted proof of export proceeds where required by the bank, customs, or foreign-exchange rules
VAT return and accounting reconciliation linking the export transaction to the relevant invoice, customs record, and payment

For offshore services: executed service agreement, deliverables, timesheets or work papers, customer location evidence, proof of offshore use, and payment records; customs documents do not ordinarily apply unless goods are also exported
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may deny or reverse zero-rating where export, nonresident-customer, offshore-use, customs, payment, or invoice evidence is incomplete or inconsistent. Denied treatment can result in assessment of the applicable VAT, late-payment charges, administrative penalties, interest, denial or recovery of input VAT refunds, and retrospective tax liabilities for the audited periods. False invoices, fictitious exports, concealed taxable supplies, fraudulent refund claims, or intentional evasion may trigger tax-evasion proceedings, monetary fines, civil recovery, and potential criminal sanctions under the VAT Law and related tax legislation. Export proceeds and foreign-exchange documentation may also be reviewed by customs, banks, and competent authorities. The 180-day period should be treated as a transaction-control deadline for repatriation evidence where applicable to the relevant export, banking, customs, or foreign-exchange rules; it is not a universal substitute for the separate VAT statutory conditions, and transaction-specific Central Bank of Egypt, banking, and customs requirements must be confirmed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - البنك المركزي المصري; exchange-control and investor-inflow coordination with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined exchange-rate regime for the EGP since March 6, 2024, replacing the prior managed band. Current-account transactions (cross-border service fees, dividends, profit repatriation) are convertible through licensed banks upon presentation of underlying contracts and, where thresholds apply, an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax-clearance certificate. Capital-account transactions (equity injection, shareholder loans, liquidation proceeds) remain canalized through licensed Egyptian banks, require Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI registration formalities, and are subject to the CBE investor currency-transfer declaration. The free-transfer guarantee of the Investment Law applies only after tax compliance and CBE documentary controls; the LLC's accumulated EGP balances cannot be re-exported without underlying commercial documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the post-March 2024 unified-rate circulars, the mandatory surrender and conversion ratio for cross-border service-export proceeds is effectively zero percent; the LLC may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in a CBE-licensed foreign-currency account. Statutory repatriation still applies: proceeds from cross-border carbon-audit services must be received into an Egyptian bank account within 180 days from the date of invoice (CBE directives during the 2022-2023 dollar-discipline phase compressed certain commodity export windows to 60-90 days, but non-oil professional services stand at the 180-day outer ceiling). Receipts must be credited through SWIFT and cannot be held offshore indefinitely without CBE approval; a service-export register with underlying contracts and signed audit reports must be maintained for the bank's repatriation due-diligence audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Foreign-Currency Account
Operational Treasury Account / USD and EUR Clearing Account / FX Hedging Desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Alexandria S.A.E. (Intesa Sanpaolo Group)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. Egypt does not recognize foreign e-money institution (EMI) licenses for holding EGP or for accessing the CBE's domestic clearing rails (IEPS/IPN). Offshore EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut-type payment gateways) may be used only as ancillary receivables collectors in USD/EUR from non-resident carbon-audit clients, subject to standard OFAC/EU sanctions screening by their partner correspondent banks; such EMIs cannot lawfully settle with Egyptian tax authorities or issue EGP-denominated receipts. The durable treasury architecture must route 100% of Egyptian-invoiced contract value to the onshore CBE-licensed account to satisfy repatriation windows; sustained EMI intermediation above USD 50,000 per month should be avoided for the Egyptian-resident entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required. At least one director or authorized signatory, or an attorney-in-fact holding a consular-legalized power of attorney in favor of a resident manager, must attend the branch for account opening. Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; corporate documents from non-Arab states require legalization by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs plus the consulate or embassy of the issuing state. CBE AML rules under Law No. 80 of 2002 mandate face-to-face identification of every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more. Remote opening is effectively unavailable for a non-resident-owned LLC; a two- to three-day in-country board and UBO visit (Cairo, Giza, or Suez Canal Economic Zone branch) is mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO at 100% ownership with no Egyptian economic substance and no prior banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consular-legalized LLC incorporation contract, GAFI and Commercial Registry extracts, certified passport copies and proof of physical presence at interview, board resolution naming authorized signatories, UBO structure chart of the parent, and statutory auditor letter confirming compliance with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company descriptor containing 'carbon,' 'offset,' or 'brokerage' triggering commodity-trading AML flagging
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541620 management-consultancy classification; executed advisory agreements defining Scope 1-3 measurement scope; proof that carbon-credit purchases are executed on explicit client instructions under an agency model; and, if the LLC acts as offset broker, registration and licensing under the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority voluntary carbon market framework (launched 2023-2024).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity on inbound USD equity injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-month corporate bank statements of the shareholder; contemporaneous contracts of the parent ESG practice evidencing revenue lineage; CBE investor currency-transfer declaration filed on inflow; sanctions-screening report confirming the entity and its UBO are absent from OFAC, EU, and UN lists; sworn declaration of no involvement in dual-use goods or restricted sectors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First outbound dividend or profit remittance flagged by bank tax-compliance control (Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 69)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ETA-issued tax card and clearance certificate; audited Egyptian financial statements; dividend-distribution board resolution; 10% dividend withholding tax settlement receipts; proof that the GAFI registration and Capital Register conditions under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 have been satisfied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire transfers to international carbon registries such as Verra or Gold Standard lacking a commodity-supporting payload
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry account statements; underlying retirement or transfer confirmation including credit serial numbers; the client's offset-brokerage mandate; bank remittance instruction showing purpose of payment as 'payment for intangible carbon-credit services'; CBE-compliant invoice and contract file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital is wired by SWIFT MT103 in USD or EUR to the LLC's foreign-currency account at the onboarding bank, referencing 'equity contribution - Investment Law No. 72 of 2017' and including the GAFI registration number. The receiving bank files the CBE investor currency-transfer declaration within five business days and mirrors the deposit into the capital-escrow ledger for issuance of the certificate of deposit required at the notary (El-Shaher El-Aqary) stage. Ongoing operational inflows from exported carbon-audit services are received by SWIFT MT103 referencing the invoice number and 'ESG advisory services - ISIC 7020'; EGP conversion takes place at the onshore interbank rate. Payment rails are restricted to wire transfer; no card-acceptance infrastructure is necessary at this treasury stage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border operational settlements (international verifier license fees, subscription software, travel, external expert fees) are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the LLC's foreign-currency account, supported by invoice, contract, and ETA clearance where requested. EGP funding for such wires is converted through the bank's dealing desk against a foreign-currency purchase contract; the bank must retain underlying commercial documents to preserve the CBE current-account standard. Commercial letters of credit are not required for service imports; for future purchases of registered carbon credits, the LLC should remit on an instructed basis against invoice and registry serialization, and any Egyptian client procuring offsets through an L/C may open a confirmed sight L/C with the LLC's delivery obligation evidenced by registry contracts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (non-speculative; bank-executed with underlying service invoices and maximum tenor of 12 months)

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP executed at the non-resident shareholder holding level through international counterparties - onshore booking requires CBE approval and is generally denied for resident entities
Cross-currency swaps with demonstrable trade or investment exposure (executable only with CBE approval and proven economic substance)
European-style FX options for transaction hedging under the post-2024 float regime (available from top-tier onshore banks where underlying exposure is evidenced)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and partners' general assembly approval minutes deposited to company file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Companies Registration Department (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit: administrative warning; persistent non-filing subject to GAFI fine under Law 4/2022 of up to EGP 10,000 and regulatory strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 21 CIT) with integrated audited financial statements and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Tax Audit Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fourth month following the end of the fiscal year (30 April for a 31 December fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 5,000 (approx. USD 100) and monthly late-payment interest at 1% on the unpaid tax; attachments of bank accounts and refusal of the annual tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the following calendar year, or within 30 days of a share transfer/change if earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under AML Law No. 80/2002 of up to EGP 300,000; referral to the Egyptian Financial Investigation Unit; potential freeze of transactions and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Licence (Trade Permit) annual renewal at the company's head-office premises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Governorate – District Commercial Licence Office (Mahala)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal before 1 January of each operating year (or on the licence anniversary date depending on governorate rules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate closure order of premises; recurring late fine of EGP 500 per month; suspension of the company's commercial registration until payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory for all Egyptian limited liability companies under Companies Law No. 4/2022 without exemption; for income tax purposes audited statements must be attached when annual gross turnover exceeds EGP 5,000,000 (approx. USD 103,000). Smaller LLCs may file an unaudited balance sheet supported by a reviewing accountant report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS), aligned with IFRS; required for preparing the legal financial statements that accompany the CIT-21 return and GAFI deposit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC manager must keep the UBO register current and file an annual confirmation with GAFI by 31 March. Any transfer of membership interests must be recorded in the members' register and notified to GAFI within 30 days of the transfer. The confirmation must certify that the recorded natural persons who ultimately own or control over 25% of the LLC remain accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (General Assembly and Management Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,000 for GAFI-sponsored registered office and annual statutory secretarial services in Cairo/Alexandria.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,000 per year for a licensed Egyptian audit firm covering financial statements, EFRS compliance, and tax attachments.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 16 'Corporate Income Tax Return' issued by the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); mandatory electronic filing via ETA e-Tax portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg (taxpayer authentication via Tax Card credentials and digital signature); the Form 16 submission in tax year 2024 must be accompanied by audited financial statements, depreciation schedules, and the annual transfer-pricing declaration.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual. In addition, an LLC must file quarterly advance CIT returns (installments) within one month after the end of each of the first three quarters, with each installment equal to 25% of the prior year's final CIT liability; the annual return reconciles all installments.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form 16 must be filed no later than 4 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 April for tax year ending 31 December; ETA may approve a different accounting period for non-resident parents upon application). Quarterly installment deadlines: 30 April, 31 July, 31 October for a calendar-year filer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 1 - Identification (Tax Card No., commercial registration, fiscal period, activity code ISIC 7020)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registrant legal details as per ETA Tax Card and Commercial Registry; principal business described as management consultancy activities - ESG and carbon footprint auditing and offset brokerage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident LLC of the same group with an Egyptian PE must enter the ETA branch tax-card registration number of its Egyptian PE and must not file as a standalone resident entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 2 - Income statement per accounting standard (revenue, COS, SGA, net profit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement data prepared under Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) / IFRS; revenue includes carbon-audit fees, assurance fees, consulting retainers, and offset brokerage commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must recognize Egyptian-source revenues booked to the Egyptian office; fees invoiced offshore for contracts performed in Egypt remain taxable in Egypt under Article 12 of Law 91/2005 business-profits source rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 3 - Tax adjustments (non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, entertainment limitation 30%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back schedule for non-deductible items and reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable profit; ETA expects deduction evidence for third-party data services, software subscriptions, and audit subcontract fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office recharges and interoffice cost allocations are deductible only up to an ETA-accepted apportionment; invoices lacking substance for tangible benefit are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 4 - Taxable income and 25% CIT computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Section computes gross tax due after Article 30 recoveries (if any); loss carryforward deduction limited to five consecutive years and restricted to the same trade/business scope.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with an Egyptian PE is taxed on the taxable profits attributable to the PE only; foreign losses of its head office cannot be deducted against PE profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 5 - Transfer-pricing schedule (intercompany revenue, costs, intangibles, financing) and TP declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separately schedules each controlled transaction category with counterparty, country, method, and arm's length outcome; required when related-party transactions exceed statutory thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border fees paid to overseas ESG-data or carbon-credits affiliates require functional and risk analysis, OECD comparability adjustments, and advance pricing agreement (APA) option with ETA for the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 6 - Tax credits, prepayments and balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly installments, foreign tax credit (FTC) for foreign WHT on the same income, and final settlement amount / refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: FTC for Egyptian-source income doubly taxed abroad requires certified foreign tax return and TRC evidence; the credit is capped at Egyptian CIT proportionally attributable to foreign income.
